title: Escape-hatch scenario planner and tactical tracker
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, minimalist "escape-hatch" planner for mid-lifecycle renewal risk that prioritizes speed over completeness. Designed for high-touch accounts where we need an executable set of plays, a compact tracker, and a one-page exec escalation brief that can be handed to customer success leadership within 60 minutes.

Audience:
CS AEs, Renewal Owners, Solutions Engineers, CSM managers, Sales leadership when an account enters formal escalation.

When to use this doc (trigger signals):
- Renewal < 90 days and NRR or adoption trend shows > 20% drop quarter-over-quarter.
- Two or more Severity-2 support issues in last 30 days tied to production latency or integration breakpoints.
- Customer expresses intent to pause or reduce spend in a QBR call or in written comms.
- Executive-level silence: no response to three sequence outreach attempts from AE and CSM in 14 days.

Outcome goals (pick 1 primary + up to 2 secondary):
1) Primary: Convert to renewal at ≥ 90% of committed ARR.
2) Secondary: Secure a 3–6 month technical remediation plan signed by customer.
3) Secondary: Preserve brand reference by arranging a keystone pilot for new feature set.

Quick-start checklist (first 60 minutes):
- Triage: Pull last 12 weeks of telemetry (latency p50/p95, error rate, API calls/day) and usage by product feature. (Owner: SE or Data Ops)
- Stake map: Confirm current contract owner, procurement lead, engineering champion, and executive sponsor. (Owner: AE)
- Recent comms: Snapshot last 6 inbound/outbound threads and calendar invites with stakeholders. (Owner: CSM)
- Risk scorecard: Fill the 9-line risk rubric (financial exposure, technical surface area impacted, exec attention, adoption velocity, workaround maturity, time to fix estimate, legal/contract friction, competitive pressure, references at risk). Use high/med/low buckets. (Owner: AE+CSM)
- Decide: If risk is high in at least 3 buckets, escalate to Rapid Stabilization (below).

Play buckets (choose up to three, run in parallel if possible):
A) Rapid Stabilization (time horizon: 1–7 days)
  - Emergency desktop: SE-led debug with dedicated GPU pool allocation, elevated priority in infra queue.
  - Temporary rollback: Switch customer to last-known-good model or plan with documented performance SLAs.
  - Manual workaround sheet: Provide short-run operational playbooks AE/CSM can hand to customer engineers.

B) Commercial Incentive (time horizon: 3–21 days)
  - Limited credit: One-time service credit tied to measurable SLA delta (e.g., 25% credit if p95 latency > threshold).
  - Conditional extension: Offer 30–90 day contract extension to allow technical remediation with no penalty.
  - Feature roadmap slot: Prioritized placement for a narrow roadmap item in exchange for commitment.

C) Leadership Engagement (time horizon: 7–30 days)
  - Exec-to-exec call: 30-min prep, with clear ask and success metrics.
  - Product advisory: Invite customer to a private product session; surface risks and co-created mitigation.
  - Reference re-framing: If reference is at risk, propose a controlled success milestone with public PR gate.

Decision thresholds & routing rules:
- If financial exposure > $250k ARR and technical severity = high => require CSM manager + AE + Sales Director + SE war room within 24 hours.
- If customer names a competitor on a renewal call or procurement states intent to source alternatives => Sales Director + CRO notification and immediate commercial hold.
- If no meaningful response from exec sponsor after 2 outreach attempts and risk = high => open legal & contract review for deferral options.

Escalation hierarchy (who to call):
- Triage lead: AE or CSM (immediate)
- SE escalation: Senior SE (on-call)
- CS manager: Regional CS Lead
- Product owner: Director, Product (hosted-api or dedicated)
- Technical exec: VP, Engineering (serving-runtime) for cross-team prioritization
- Commercial exec: VP, Revenue Operations for discount approvals

Tactical tracker (one-line-per-action, use copies in Slack #renewal-saves):
Columns: action-id | owner | action | due | status | impact-estimate | notes
Example row (as text):
RS-01 | Marcus Lee | Provision isolated GPU queue and shift to G1-legacy model | 2026-02-24 | in_progress | latency p95 -> -40% | temp rollback executed; customer aware

Email templates (copy/paste, rewrite tone as needed):
- Exec ask: short and precise
Subject: Request: 30m exec sync to align on renewal support plan
Hi [Exec name],
We value our partnership and want to ensure you have an uninterrupted path forward. We have a short remediation plan for the production issues you raised and would like to confirm next steps and a timeline to avoid disruption at renewal. Can you join a 30-minute call this week? Proposed times: [2 options].
Thanks,
[AE name]

- Remediation confirmation to implementation team
Hi team,
Per our rapid stabilization plan, we will route [customer] to model X (GG-2024-g) on the dedicated pool S-2 at 09:00 UTC tomorrow. SEs: please validate KV cache warmup and confirm backchannel when done. Tracker: RS-02.

Metrics & monitoring to present in QBR and during save sprint:
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 for generate and embeddings calls (7d, 30d baselines).
- Usage: daily active API keys, tokens/day, peak concurrent sessions.
- Error surface: 5xx rate by endpoint, top 3 stack traces.
- Business signals: feature adoption rate, revenue churn signal, number of seats added/removed in last 90 days.

Simulation exercise (30–90 minute dry run):
Objective: Practice run of the escape-hatch for a hypothetical 500k ARR account where inference latency increased by 300% after a model swap.
Steps:
1) 10 min: quick data pull - telemetry and contract snapshot.
2) 15 min: play selection and assignment.
3) 30 min: execution - SE does rollback, AE drafts credits email, exec prep doc assembled.
4) 15 min: debrief - what broke, who was missing, 1 action to improve next run.
Deliverable: burn-down tracker and a one-paragraph exec brief.

One-page Exec Brief template (max 300 words):
- Headline: "At-risk: [Customer] — Renewal in [X days] — Primary ask: [e.g., 30-day remediation + keep book]"
- Situation: 3-sentence summary of what happened and impact.
- Actions taken: 4 bullets, with owners and status.
- Ask of execs: 1) Time for 30-minute call; 2) Approval for up to [X] credits; 3) Priority for product fix by [date].
- KPIs to restore: p95 latency target, daily active keys, sign-off milestone.

Post-save playbook (after we close the renewal):
- 30-day stabilization retro: 1-2 engineers assigned to SLA watch for next 30 days.
- Commitment ladder: staged deliverables with clear acceptance tests.
- Compensation reconciliation: finalize credit or contract amendment and log to finance.
- Reference rehabilitation: 90-day milestone and customer case study opportunity if delivered.

Known constraints and guardrails:
- Never promise SLA-level credits without Sales Ops approval.
- Rolling back to older models requires a performance test window — coordinate with infra for warmup.
- Do not gift unbounded roadmap work; frame offers as time-boxed prioritized slots.

Open questions for leadership: (to surface in weekly CS leadership sync)
- Is the company comfortable with a standardized credit table by bucket (small/medium/large) or do we require case-by-case approvals?
- Should we centralize the dedicated pool pre-allocations for high-touch accounts to speed fast rollbacks?

Attachments & artifacts to collect during a save sprint:
- Telemetry export (CSV) for last 90 days
- Contract summary sheet (signed pages and renewal date)
- Recent NPS/CSAT notes and last QBR deck
- Slack export for named exec comms

Next steps (for the current save instance):
1) Fill the risk scorecard and post to #renewal-saves (Owner: AE) — timeline: 1 hour.
2) Provision war room (Zoom + shared doc) and assign RS- actions (Owner: CS Manager) — timeline: 4 hours.
3) Lock-in exec call if needed (Owner: AE) — timeline: 24 hours.
4) Postmortem and update template with 1 improvement (Owner: CSM) — timeline: 7 days after stabilization.

Notes to self / Constraints while drafting:
- Keep templates short — we want copy/paste readiness.
- Prioritize measurable asks (time, credit, product slot) over vague promises.
- This document is intentionally terse; expand sections into separate SOPs once a pattern repeats.

End of document.

Revision history (quick):
- 2025-11-02 initial sketch by Priya Anand
- 2025-12-12 added decision thresholds and tracker example (Marcus Lee)
- 2026-02-20 formalized exec brief template and simulation exercise (Olivia Grant)
